company.name: AI Impact Evaluation
company.tagline: AI-native Software Engineering Intelligence: one trustworthy, real-time answer to how healthy your delivery is and what your AI investment returns.
company.description: AI Impact Evaluation is a multi-tenant, event-driven Software Engineering Intelligence (SEI) platform. Teams connect their existing tools once and the platform ingests data from source control (GitHub/GitLab), project management (Jira), CI/CD (GitHub Actions/Jenkins), code quality (SonarQube), incident management (PagerDuty/Opsgenie), and AI coding assistants (Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code). It normalizes contributor identities and team structures, then computes DORA and SPACE-aligned metrics on a materialized semantic layer with zero manual tagging. Results are served through role-based drill-down dashboards for Executives, Managers, and ICs, plus exportable board-ready reports and (Phase 3) AI adoption/ROI analytics and an automated first-pass code-review agent. Architecture is five layers: Sources -> Ingestion (queue-isolated connectors) -> Identity & Normalization -> Metrics/Semantic layer -> Application/API -> Presentation. Connectors are isolated behind a message queue so a vendor API outage degrades gracefully and never loses events. It is strictly an analytics layer over the toolchain and never replaces Jira/GitHub/CI.
company.objective: Over 30 days a candidate should demonstrate they can extend an event-driven analytics platform end to end: build and harden queue-isolated connectors with idempotent, replay-safe ingestion; reconcile contributor identities and team structures; implement DORA metric computations (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR) correctly from tool events with no manual tagging; expose role-scoped, RBAC-enforced dashboard APIs; and ship the frontend drill-down and export surfaces. Throughout, they must respect the platform's non-negotiable rules: no surveillance features, no manual-tagging dependency, analytics-layer-only, least-privilege integrations, and full auditability. Documentation (ADRs, architecture doc, metric definitions, OpenAPI, CHANGELOG) is part of the definition of done for every change.
company.domainDetails: SEI platforms live or die on metric trust. Three principles govern everything: (1) Trust over surveillance -- no keystroke, idle-time, or activity-monitoring metric may exist or be derivable; individual views are opt-in and growth-framed, never leaderboards. (2) Zero-tagging automation -- every metric derives automatically from tool events; engineers never change how they work. (3) Metric transparency -- every metric ships with a published definition and formula. DORA metrics are computed at repo, org, and team scope; team rollups are computed from raw per-event rows joined to team-repo membership, never by averaging repo-day medians (averaging medians is statistically wrong for percentiles). Lead time is reported as median (p50/p75/p90), never mean. Failures for CFR/MTTR come from incident linkage or hotfix/rollback heuristics, with confidence badges when heuristic-based. Freshness target is <=15 minutes from source event to materialized metric; dashboards load <3s at ~1M events; time-to-first-insight target is <30 minutes from first connection.

techStack.backend: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 (Web, Data JPA, Security)
techStack.testing: JUnit + Spring Boot Test (backend), Vitest (frontend), recorded API fixtures for connectors

tickets.title: Onboarding: run the platform locally and trace one event end-to-end
tickets.description: Get the monorepo running via docker-compose (Postgres with staging/core/mart schemas, RabbitMQ, api-core, metrics-engine, identity-service, a connector, and the React frontend). Read docs/03-architecture/system-architecture.md and docs/02-standards/engineering-standards.md first -- code that contradicts them is rejected. Then follow a single GitHub webhook event through the pipeline: connector -> queue -> ingestion writer -> staging.raw_event -> identity-service -> core -> metrics-engine -> mart -> api-core -> dashboard. Write down where the event lands at each hop.
acceptanceCriteria: All services start via docker-compose and the frontend renders the Cockpit shell
You can name the queue topic, the staging idempotency key, and the mart table a metric lands in
You have read the architecture doc and engineering standards and can state the five non-negotiable product rules

tickets.title: Verify GitHub webhook signatures in the GitHub connector
tickets.description: The GitHub connector must reject any inbound webhook whose HMAC-SHA256 signature (X-Hub-Signature-256) does not match the shared secret before the payload is wrapped in an event envelope and published to the queue. Secret comes from an env var / secret manager -- never from code or config. Invalid signatures return 401 and are counted, never enqueued.
acceptanceCriteria: Requests with a missing or wrong X-Hub-Signature-256 are rejected with 401 and never published to the queue
Signature comparison is constant-time; the secret is read from an env var / secret manager
Unit tests cover valid, invalid, and missing-signature cases against recorded fixtures

tickets.title: Wrap connector payloads in the standard event envelope (ADR-0003)
tickets.description: Every connector must publish to the queue using the standard envelope {source, sourceId, eventType, receivedAt, connectorVersion, payload} defined in ADR-0003. Refactor the GitHub connector's publish path to build this envelope consistently for PR, commit, and workflow_run events. If the envelope contract changes, ADR-0003 and the architecture doc must be updated in the same PR.
acceptanceCriteria: All published events use the {source, sourceId, eventType, receivedAt, connectorVersion, payload} envelope
eventType clearly distinguishes PR, commit, and workflow_run events
Envelope construction is covered by tests; no business logic leaks into the connector

tickets.title: Idempotent staging writes in the Ingestion Writer
tickets.description: The Ingestion Writer is the sole writer to staging. It must insert each event idempotently on (source, sourceId, eventType) so that webhook re-delivery and backfill replay never create duplicate staging rows. Staging is immutable and append-only. Poison messages that repeatedly fail must be routed to the dead-letter queue, not retried forever.
acceptanceCriteria: Re-delivering the same event yields exactly one staging.raw_event row (idempotent on source+sourceId+eventType)
Poison messages are routed to the DLQ after bounded retries
Replaying a backfill batch over existing data produces no duplicates

tickets.title: Rate-limit-aware backfill polling for the GitHub connector
tickets.description: On first connect the connector backfills historical PRs, commits, and workflow runs. It must honor GitHub's rate-limit headers and Retry-After, backing off and queue-and-draining rather than dropping events. Backfill progress must be visible so the Admin can see it advancing toward the 30-minute time-to-value target.
acceptanceCriteria: Connector honors rate-limit / Retry-After headers and backs off without dropping events
Backfill is resumable and idempotent (no duplicate events on retry)
Backfill progress is exposed for the Admin setup checklist

tickets.title: Jira connector: ingest issues with status-change changelogs
tickets.description: Add Jira issue ingestion (epics, stories, sprints) including the full status-change history (changelog) needed for ticket lead time. Non-standard workflows must be tolerated and reported, never rejected. Publish under the standard envelope with source='jira'. Request only least-privilege read scopes.
acceptanceCriteria: Issues ingest with their status-transition changelog within the freshness target
Non-standard workflows are tolerated and surfaced, not dropped
Only least-privilege read scopes are requested; integration tests run against recorded Jira fixtures

tickets.title: Contributor identity reconciliation across tools
tickets.description: One human is v.sharma in Git, 'Vishal S' in Jira, and vishal@ in CI. The identity-service must resolve multiple tool identities to a single canonical contributor using email/name/user-ID heuristics with confidence scoring, detect bot accounts, and fall back to git signatures. Unresolved identities are flagged for Admin review -- never silently dropped or double-counted.
acceptanceCriteria: Multiple tool identities for one person resolve to a single canonical contributor with a confidence score
Bot accounts are detected and excluded from people-dimension metrics by default
Unresolved identities are flagged for review, never dropped or double-counted

tickets.title: Team-structure import and team-repo membership
tickets.description: Import the org > team > sub-team hierarchy from GitHub org teams (members + repos) and upsert core.team, core.team_repo, and core.team_member, resolving members through the identity resolver. Team-repo membership is what later lets the metrics engine compute team-scoped DORA rollups. Teams without a source-of-record can be created manually.
acceptanceCriteria: Org teams, members, and repos import into core.team / core.team_repo / core.team_member
Members are resolved through the identity resolver, not stored as raw tool handles
Teams lacking a source-of-record can be created manually

tickets.title: DORA-1: deployment frequency at repo, org, and team scope
tickets.description: Compute deployment frequency as the count of successful production deployment events per day/week per scope. Production deployments are detected per-repo via the configurable deploy workflow pattern (METRICS_DEPLOY_WORKFLOW_PATTERN) -- no manual tagging. Failed/cancelled deployments are excluded from the count. Materialize into mart.metric_daily with scope_id/scope_type. Add the metric definition to docs/01-product/metric-definitions.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Deployment frequency computes at repo, org, and team scope into mart.metric_daily
Failed/cancelled deployments are excluded; rollbacks count as deploys but are flagged for CFR
A metric definition (formula, sources, edge cases, BRD ref) is added to metric-definitions.md

tickets.title: DORA-2: lead time for changes (median, with p75/p90)
tickets.description: For each PR included in a deployment, lead time = deploy_finished_at - min(authored_at of commits unique to the PR). Report the median (p50) with p75/p90 available; means are never used. Handle squash/rebase (use pre-merge PR commit history), force-pushed branches (earliest surviving authored time), and cap stale authored dates >90 days with a UI flag rather than skewing the median.
acceptanceCriteria: Lead time reports p50/p75/p90 (never mean) per scope
Squash/rebase and force-push edge cases use the correct authored timestamps
Authored dates >90 days are capped and flagged, and unit tests cover each edge case

tickets.title: Team-scope percentiles from raw events, not median-of-medians
tickets.description: A subtle correctness bug: team-scoped percentile metrics (lead time, MTTR, PR cycle time) must be computed from the underlying per-event population joined via core.team_repo -- NOT by averaging repo-day medians. Averaging medians does not yield the team's true median. Refactor the team rollup path to aggregate raw rows and add a regression test proving the two approaches differ.
acceptanceCriteria: Team percentile metrics are computed from the raw per-event population, never from repo-day medians
A regression test constructs data where median-of-medians differs from the true median and asserts the correct value
The behavior is documented in the metric definition's edge cases

tickets.title: DORA-3: change failure rate from hotfix/rollback heuristics
tickets.description: CFR = failed_deployments / total_deployments over the window. A deployment is failed if within 48h it is followed by a rollback event or a hotfix deploy (branch hotfix/*, label hotfix) touching the same deployable unit. Until the incident connector ships, display a 'heuristic-based' confidence badge. A rollback deploy is itself excluded from the failure numerator (it is the remediation). Detection patterns are per-repo configurable.
acceptanceCriteria: CFR computes from rollback/hotfix heuristics within a 48h window and shows a heuristic-confidence badge
A rollback deploy is excluded from the failure numerator; multiple failure signals for one deploy count once
Deploy/hotfix detection patterns are per-repo configurable via env

tickets.title: DORA-4: MTTR (median restore time)
tickets.description: MTTR (median) MVP heuristic = remediation_deploy_finished_at - failed_deploy_finished_at for deployments marked failed by DORA-3. Keep the name MTTR for industry familiarity though the statistic is the median. Cascading hotfix chains attribute failure to the earliest deploy in the chain. Design the code so the Phase-2 incident-based formula (incident_resolved_at - incident_opened_at) can slot in without a rewrite.
acceptanceCriteria: MTTR reports the median restore time for heuristic-failed deployments
Cascading hotfix chains attribute failure to the earliest deploy
The computation is structured so the incident-based formula can replace the heuristic without a rewrite

tickets.title: Incremental metric recompute within the 15-minute freshness target
tickets.description: The metrics engine must incrementally recompute only the affected metric windows when new events land, keeping end-to-end lag (source event -> materialized mart) under 15 minutes. Recompute must be reproducible from staging: the same input always yields the same output, and the metric logic version is recorded with each value.
acceptanceCriteria: Only affected windows recompute on new events; end-to-end lag stays under 15 minutes in a load smoke test
Recompute from staging is deterministic and reproducible
Each materialized value records the metric logic version that produced it

tickets.title: Cockpit API: headline metrics with a freshness indicator
tickets.description: Implement GET /api/v1/metrics/cockpit?scope=<id> returning headline DORA metrics plus PR velocity for a repo, org (*), or team UUID, each with current value, trend, target band, and a data-freshness timestamp. Update the OpenAPI spec before implementing (APIs are contract-first). Empty results must explain why (no data / out of range / still ingesting), never return a blank payload.
acceptanceCriteria: The endpoint serves repo, org, and team scope with value, trend, target band, and freshness timestamp
OpenAPI spec is updated before the endpoint change and matches the response
Empty results carry an explanatory reason code rather than a blank payload

tickets.title: Cockpit UI: real tiles with loading/error/empty states and inline definitions
tickets.description: Wire the React Cockpit to /api/v1/metrics/cockpit. Each tile shows the metric value, trend, RAG status against its target band, and its plain-language definition on hover (metric transparency is a trust requirement). Implement explicit loading, error, and empty states -- an empty chart must explain itself. Must render within 3s at ~1M events.
acceptanceCriteria: Tiles render real metrics with RAG status and an inline definition on hover
Loading, error, and empty states are implemented and self-explanatory
Cockpit renders within the 3s performance budget

tickets.title: Org -> team drill-down preserving filters and breadcrumbs
tickets.description: Add GET /api/v1/teams for the team picker and let the Cockpit drill from org into team-scoped tiles. Drill-down must preserve the active date/scope filters and provide breadcrumbs to navigate back up. Individual-level drill-down is out of scope here and must remain gated by RBAC AND personal opt-in (E8-S2).
acceptanceCriteria: Drill-down from org to team preserves active filters and time range
Breadcrumbs navigate back up the scope hierarchy
No individual-level drill-down is exposed without opt-in gating

tickets.title: Enforce five-role RBAC on every metrics and admin endpoint
tickets.description: api-core is an RS256 JWT resource server (ADR-0004). The five roles ADMIN, ENG_LEADER, MANAGER, IC, FINANCE_READONLY must enforce their default visibility on every request. Gate /api/v1/metrics/** to analytical roles (IC denied org/team metrics), and /api/v1/audit/** and /api/v1/admin/** to ADMIN. No path -- including exports and deep links -- may leak data outside the caller's scope. Run the OWASP Top 10 checklist for each endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: All five roles enforce default visibility server-side; IC is denied org/team metrics
Admin and audit endpoints are ADMIN-only; no export or deep link leaks out-of-scope data
An OWASP Top 10 review is recorded for the changed endpoints and access changes are audited

tickets.title: Append-only, tamper-evident audit log with admin-only read
tickets.description: Every configuration change, access grant, and data export must be written to an append-only audit log capturing actor, timestamp, and target, retrievable for >=12 months. Reads are ADMIN-only. Lay the groundwork for cryptographic tamper-evidence (hash chaining) even if full hardening comes later. Wire the Admin console to GET /api/v1/audit.
acceptanceCriteria: Config changes, access grants, and exports are written to the append-only audit log with actor/timestamp/target
Audit reads are ADMIN-only and retained >=12 months
A tamper-evidence approach (e.g. hash chaining) is designed and documented

tickets.title: Presentation-ready export reflecting current filters
tickets.description: Executives export a shareable, formatted artifact (PDF/deck-ready) reflecting the current filters, completing in seconds, with metric definitions attached. Every export emits a report_exported event and an audit-log entry. The export must respect the caller's access scope -- it can never contain data the viewer could not see on screen.
acceptanceCriteria: Export reflects active filters, attaches metric definitions, and completes in seconds
Each export emits report_exported and an audit entry
Export contents never exceed the caller's access scope

tickets.title: 30-minute time-to-value: setup status checklist
tickets.description: Implement GET /api/v1/setup/status (ADMIN/ENG_LEADER) deriving a four-item checklist (git / ticketing / CI / dashboard connected) and a firstConnectionAt -> firstDashboardAt minutesToValue figure entirely from staging.raw_event and mart.metric_daily timestamps -- no manual flags. When no events/metrics exist yet, minutesToValue and withinTarget stay null (never a misleading 0).
acceptanceCriteria: The checklist and minutesToValue derive purely from existing staging/mart timestamps
withinTarget = minutesToValue <= 30; both stay null until any event/metric exists
The figure is org-wide, not per-user, and the frontend Setup view renders it

tickets.title: PR review analytics: size, turnaround, and reviewer balance
tickets.description: Compute PR size distribution (additions+deletions; oversized default >400 lines), review turnaround, and reviewer workload shown as BALANCE across the team -- never an individual leaderboard. This requires ingesting PR review events. Respect access scope and the non-surveillance / growth-framed principle throughout.
acceptanceCriteria: PR size, review turnaround, and reviewer load compute per team/repo
Reviewer load is presented as balance, never as an individual ranking
Views respect access scope and the non-surveillance principle

tickets.title: Proactive flags for oversized / aging PRs
tickets.description: Flag open PRs that exceed configurable size or age thresholds (stale = no activity >7 days; oversized >400 lines by default) so a tech lead is alerted before release is blocked. Acting on a flag emits pr_flag_actioned. Thresholds are team-configurable with sensible defaults.
acceptanceCriteria: PRs exceeding size/age thresholds are flagged in-product with team-configurable thresholds
Acting on a flag emits pr_flag_actioned
Sensible defaults (>400 lines, >7 days) apply when unset

tickets.title: Investment Profile: planned vs unplanned vs rework classification
tickets.description: Correlate Git activity to Jira epics to classify each unit of work as planned, unplanned, or rework using linkage heuristics (branch names, PR titles, smart commits). Show the split per team over time with category definitions; unclassifiable work goes to a transparent bucket, never silently dropped. Document the methodology so it is auditable.
acceptanceCriteria: Work classifies into planned / unplanned / rework via Jira<->Git linkage heuristics
The split is shown per team over time with visible category definitions
Unclassifiable work is bucketed transparently and the methodology is documented

tickets.title: Goals & OKR tracking bound to a metric
tickets.description: Let a leader bind a goal to a metric, target value, scope, and time window, with multiple concurrent goals per team (emits goal_created). Progress recomputes automatically as metrics refresh within the freshness target, showing on-track / at-risk / off-track against the target trajectory, surfaced in the Cockpit for in-scope leaders.
acceptanceCriteria: A goal binds to a metric, target, scope, and window; multiple concurrent goals per team are supported
Progress recomputes automatically and shows on-track / at-risk / off-track
goal_created is emitted and in-scope leaders see progress in the Cockpit

tickets.title: AI-assisted work detection from commit trailers
tickets.description: Detect AI-assisted commits/PRs from assistant telemetry and/or commit-trailer conventions (Copilot/Claude/Cursor), computing adoption rate = distinct(engineers with AI attribution) / distinct(active engineers) per team and org. Detection method and confidence must be shown alongside the number; low-confidence attribution is labeled, never silently folded into the total.
acceptanceCriteria: Adoption rate computes per team and org from telemetry and/or commit-trailer conventions
Detection method and confidence are displayed with the figure
Low-confidence attribution is labeled, not silently included

tickets.title: AI vs non-AI delta with visible methodology caveats
tickets.description: Compare cycle time, change failure rate, and rework side by side for AI-assisted vs non-AI-assisted work in the same window, segmenting existing DORA-2/DORA-3 and rework computations by the AI-attribution flag. Confounder caveats (team mix, PR-size mix) must be surfaced in the UI -- comparisons must never claim causation.
acceptanceCriteria: Cycle time, CFR, and rework are compared for AI vs non-AI work in the same window
Methodology and confounder caveats are surfaced in-UI
No comparison claims causation

tickets.title: Dollar AI ROI figure with adjustable assumptions
tickets.description: Produce an estimated monthly value recovered vs AI spend: estimated_hours_saved = ai_assisted_pr_count * (nonAi_cycle_time_p50 - ai_assisted_cycle_time_p50); dollar_value = estimated_hours_saved * blended_hourly_rate; roi_multiple = dollar_value / total_ai_spend. blended_hourly_rate and attribution method are org-configurable assumptions shown alongside the figure -- never a hidden constant.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one assistant yields a dollar ROI figure and an roi_multiple
blended_hourly_rate and attribution method are configurable and shown alongside the figure
Assumptions are never presented as hidden constants

tickets.title: AI code-review agent: advisory first-pass comments (per-repo toggle)
tickets.description: On PR open, an isolated agent service posts advisory comments (style, likely bugs, security) clearly attributed to the agent -- humans remain the deciders. This is the one allowed exception to the analytics-layer-only rule (it writes PR comments). It must be enable/disable per repository and default off. Requires an ADR before adoption of the LLM framework.
acceptanceCriteria: On PR open the agent posts advisory, clearly-attributed comments; humans remain the deciders
The agent is enable/disable per repository and defaults off
An ADR records the LLM framework decision before adoption

tickets.title: Pre-built report library (no query language required)
tickets.description: Ship a library of pre-built reports covering the most common use cases (cycle time, bug resolution, DORA workflow) that are filterable and exportable with no query language required. Reports respect access scope and attach metric definitions. Close out the 30-day pack by verifying the documentation checklist: architecture doc current, ADRs written, READMEs current, OpenAPI current, metric definitions current, CHANGELOG updated.
acceptanceCriteria: Common-use-case reports are available, filterable, and exportable without any query language
Reports respect access scope and attach metric definitions
The documentation definition-of-done checklist passes for all shipped work

dsaProblems.title: Two Sum
dsaProblems.prompt: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Each input has exactly one solution and you may not use the same element twice. Aim for O(n) time using a hash map.

dsaProblems.title: Valid HMAC Window (Two Pointers)
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a string, determine whether it is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring case. Return true or false. Use two pointers from both ends. (Models constant-time-ish header comparison intuition.)
dsaProblems.example: s = 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama' -> true

dsaProblems.title: Group Events by Type
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a list of event-type strings, group anagrams... instead: given a list of envelope keys of the form 'source:eventType', group and return the sourceIds grouped by (source, eventType). Order within a group does not matter. Practice building composite-key maps like the ingestion envelope.

dsaProblems.title: Deduplicate by Composite Key
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a stream of records each with (source, sourceId, eventType), return the records with duplicates removed, keeping first occurrence order. This models idempotent staging inserts keyed on the triple.

dsaProblems.title: Token-Bucket Rate Limiter
dsaProblems.prompt: Design a rate limiter that allows at most N requests per rolling window of W seconds. Implement allow(timestamp) returning true if the request is permitted. Use a queue of timestamps or a token-bucket. Models rate-limit-aware connector polling.
dsaProblems.example: N=2, W=1: allow(0)=true, allow(0.1)=true, allow(0.2)=false, allow(1.2)=true

dsaProblems.title: Merge Status-Change Intervals
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a list of [start, end] intervals representing the periods a Jira ticket spent in 'in-progress' status, merge overlapping intervals and return the total in-progress duration. Sort by start, then sweep.

dsaProblems.title: Union-Find Identity Merge
dsaProblems.prompt: Given pairs of tool identities known to be the same person (e.g. ('git:vsharma','jira:VishalS')), group all identities into canonical contributors. Implement union-find with path compression and return the number of distinct people and their groups.

dsaProblems.title: Org Hierarchy Rollup
dsaProblems.prompt: Given an org > team > sub-team tree where each leaf team has a repo count, compute the total repo count for every node (a node's total = sum of its subtree). Return the totals via DFS. Models team-structure rollups.

dsaProblems.title: Count Deploys Per Day
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a list of successful-deploy epoch timestamps and a timezone offset, bucket them by calendar day and return a map of day -> count. Excludes nothing here; models deployment-frequency bucketing.

dsaProblems.title: Running Median (Two Heaps)
dsaProblems.prompt: Implement a data structure that supports addNum(x) and findMedian() in O(log n) add and O(1) median, using a max-heap and min-heap. This is exactly how lead-time p50 is maintained over a stream of PR lead times.

dsaProblems.title: Median of Combined Populations
dsaProblems.prompt: Given several sorted arrays of per-repo lead times, compute the true median of ALL values combined. Show that averaging the per-array medians can differ from the combined median. Return the correct combined median. Models the median-of-medians bug fix.
dsaProblems.example: [[1,2,3],[100]] combined median = 2.5; average of medians (2 and 100) = 51 -- wrong

dsaProblems.title: Match Hotfix to Deploy in Window
dsaProblems.prompt: Given sorted deploy timestamps and sorted hotfix timestamps, for each deploy determine if a hotfix on the same repo occurs within 48h after it. Return the count of failed deploys. Use a two-pointer sweep. Each hotfix marks at most one earliest deploy.

dsaProblems.title: Collapse Cascading Hotfix Chain
dsaProblems.prompt: Given directed links deploy -> remediating-hotfix-deploy (which may itself be remediated), attribute each failure chain to the earliest deploy and compute the restore time = last_remediation_time - earliest_deploy_time. Traverse each chain once.

dsaProblems.title: Affected Windows on New Event
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a new event timestamp and a set of daily/weekly metric window definitions, return exactly the windows that must be recomputed (those containing the timestamp). Avoid recomputing untouched windows. Models incremental recompute.
dsaProblems.example: event at day-3 -> recompute {day-3, week-1} but not day-1, day-2

dsaProblems.title: LRU Cache
dsaProblems.prompt: Implement an LRU cache with O(1) get and put using a hash map + doubly linked list. Model caching of recently requested cockpit scope responses.

dsaProblems.title: Top-K Slowest Stages
dsaProblems.prompt: Given lead-time stage durations per team, return the top-K slowest stages overall using a min-heap of size K. Models emphasizing the slowest lead-time stage on the dashboard.

dsaProblems.title: Breadcrumb Path in Scope Tree
dsaProblems.prompt: Given the org>team>sub-team tree and a target node id, return the path from the root to that node (the breadcrumb trail). Return empty if not found.

dsaProblems.title: Role-Scope Access Filter
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a user's role and scope and a requested scope id, return whether access is allowed under the rules: ADMIN=all, ENG_LEADER=org+any team, MANAGER=own teams only, IC=self only, FINANCE_READONLY=aggregated only. Return allow/deny. Models RBAC visibility filtering.

dsaProblems.title: Hash-Chained Audit Log
dsaProblems.prompt: Implement an append-only log where each entry stores hash(prev_hash + entry_data). Implement append(entry) and verify() that returns the index of the first tampered entry or -1 if intact. Models a tamper-evident audit log.
dsaProblems.example: append 3 entries, mutate entry 1 -> verify() returns 1

dsaProblems.title: Filter Export Rows by Scope
dsaProblems.prompt: Given export rows each tagged with a scope id and a set of scopes the caller may see, return only the rows within the caller's scope. Ensures an export never contains out-of-scope data.
dsaProblems.example: rows scopes=[t1,t2,t3], allowed={t1,t3} -> keep t1,t3 rows

dsaProblems.title: Minutes-To-Value From Timestamps
dsaProblems.prompt: Given raw_event received_at timestamps (with source) and metric computed_at timestamps, compute minutesToValue = min(computed_at) - min(received_at where source in {github,jira}). Return null if either side is empty (never 0).

dsaProblems.title: Balanced Reviewer Assignment
dsaProblems.prompt: Given open PRs and a set of reviewers with current loads, assign each PR to the least-loaded eligible reviewer using a min-heap, so load stays balanced (not ranked). Return the final load per reviewer.
dsaProblems.example: reviewers loads {a:0,b:0}, 3 PRs -> a:2,b:1 (or balanced equivalent)

dsaProblems.title: Flag Stale / Oversized PRs
dsaProblems.prompt: Given open PRs with (ageDays, changedLines) and thresholds (staleDays, maxLines), return the PRs that should be flagged (age > staleDays OR lines > maxLines). Models proactive PR flagging.

dsaProblems.title: Classify Work by Linkage
dsaProblems.prompt: Given PRs with branch names / titles, classify each as planned (references an epic key like PROJ-123), rework (branch matches hotfix/* or revert), or unplanned (no epic link). Unmatched goes to an 'unclassified' bucket. Return counts per category.

dsaProblems.title: Goal Progress Trajectory
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a goal (start value, target value, start date, end date) and the current value/date, classify progress as on-track, at-risk, or off-track by comparing actual vs the linear expected value for today. Return the status.
dsaProblems.example: 0->100 over 10 days, day 5 value 40 -> expected 50 -> at-risk

dsaProblems.title: Adoption Rate Over Distinct Sets
dsaProblems.prompt: Given commits tagged with author and an ai-attribution flag, compute adoption = |distinct authors with any AI-attributed commit| / |distinct active authors|. Return the ratio per team.

dsaProblems.title: Segmented Percentile Comparison
dsaProblems.prompt: Given PR cycle times each flagged AI-assisted or not, compute the p50 cycle time for each segment independently and return the delta (nonAI_p50 - AI_p50). Do not pool the segments. Models the AI-vs-non-AI delta.

dsaProblems.title: ROI Estimator
dsaProblems.prompt: Given ai_assisted_pr_count, nonAi_cycle_p50, ai_cycle_p50, blended_hourly_rate, and total_ai_spend, compute hours_saved = count*(nonAi-ai), dollar_value = hours_saved*rate, and roi_multiple = dollar_value/total_ai_spend. Return all three.
dsaProblems.example: count=100, delta=1h, rate=$80, spend=$2000 -> saved=100h, value=$8000, roi=4.0

dsaProblems.title: Rate-Limited Review Agent Dispatch
dsaProblems.prompt: PR-open events arrive faster than the review agent's per-minute LLM budget. Implement a bounded queue that dispatches up to B agent calls per minute and defers the rest to the next minute, preserving order. Return the minute each PR is processed.
dsaProblems.example: B=1, PRs at minute 0:[p1,p2,p3] -> p1@0, p2@1, p3@2

dsaProblems.title: Compose a Report from Saved Filters
dsaProblems.prompt: Given a report definition (metric, scope, date window, filters) and a metric-daily dataset, return the filtered, aggregated rows that back the report -- with no query language, just applying the structured filter object. Return empty-with-reason if nothing matches.
dsaProblems.example: report{metric:leadTime,scope:t1,window:7d} -> rows for t1 in last 7 days

quizQuestions.question: Which four metrics make up the DORA set?
options: Velocity, story points, burndown, cycle time
Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, MTTR
Code coverage, defect density, churn, throughput
quizQuestions.explanation: DORA = deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, and mean time to restore (MTTR).

quizQuestions.question: Which feature is explicitly and permanently forbidden in this platform?
quizQuestions.explanation: No surveillance features (keystroke/idle-time/screen monitoring) may exist -- an explicit ethical exclusion (BRD 5.3).

quizQuestions.question: Why is lead time reported as a median (p50) rather than a mean?
options: Medians are faster to compute than means
The mean is outlier-dominated and would misrepresent typical lead time
quizQuestions.explanation: Lead-time distributions are skewed; a few very long changes dominate the mean, so the median (p50, with p75/p90) is used.

quizQuestions.question: How must a team-scoped percentile metric (e.g. lead time) be computed?
options: By averaging each repo's daily median
By taking the maximum repo median
From the raw per-event population joined via team-repo membership
By summing repo medians and dividing by repo count
quizQuestions.explanation: Averaging repo-day medians does not yield the team's true median; team percentiles must come from the raw per-event population joined via core.team_repo.

quizQuestions.question: Why are connectors isolated behind a message queue?
options: To let engineers write to Jira from the platform
So a vendor API outage degrades gracefully and never loses events
quizQuestions.explanation: Queue isolation (retry/DLQ) means a vendor 429/5xx just queues events; nothing downstream notices the outage and no events are lost.

quizQuestions.question: On what key does the Ingestion Writer insert idempotently into staging?
quizQuestions.explanation: Idempotent insert on (source, sourceId, eventType) makes webhook re-delivery and backfill replay safe -- no duplicate staging rows.

quizQuestions.question: What is the backend technology stack?
quizQuestions.explanation: Backend is Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 (Web, Data JPA, Security) per ADR-0001.

quizQuestions.question: Which datastore backs the MVP, and how is it organized?
options: MongoDB with one collection per tool
PostgreSQL 16 with staging, core, and mart schemas
MySQL with a single flat table
quizQuestions.explanation: A single PostgreSQL 16 instance with three schemas (staging/core/mart) per ADR-0002; the split preserves a migration path to a dedicated analytical store later.

quizQuestions.question: In the MVP, how is a deployment marked as a 'failure' for change failure rate?
options: A human manually tags the deploy as failed
A rollback or hotfix deploy on the same unit within 48h (heuristic, badged)
Any deploy that took longer than average
quizQuestions.explanation: Until the incident connector ships, CFR uses rollback/hotfix heuristics within 48h and is shown with a heuristic-confidence badge -- no manual tagging.

quizQuestions.question: What is the target end-to-end metric freshness (source event to materialized metric)?
quizQuestions.explanation: The freshness target is <=15 minutes from a source event to the metric being materialized in the mart.

quizQuestions.question: What is the time-to-first-insight target after connecting the first tools?
quizQuestions.explanation: After the first Git + ticketing connection, at least one populated dashboard should render within 30 minutes (E1-S5).

quizQuestions.question: Which are the five RBAC roles enforced in api-core?
quizQuestions.explanation: The five roles are ADMIN, ENG_LEADER, MANAGER, IC, and FINANCE_READONLY (ADR-0004).

quizQuestions.question: How does api-core authenticate requests?
options: As an RS256 JWT resource server (OIDC/JWT)
Basic auth with a shared password
quizQuestions.explanation: api-core is an RS256 JWT resource server (OIDC + JWT) enforcing RBAC on every request (ADR-0004).

quizQuestions.question: What is the one allowed exception to the 'never write back to external tools' rule?
options: The Phase 3 AI review agent posting advisory PR comments
quizQuestions.explanation: The platform is an analytics layer only; the sole exception is the Phase 3 AI review agent posting PR comments.

quizQuestions.question: How is the start point of DORA-2 lead time defined in v1?
options: When the ticket was created in Jira
The authored time of the earliest commit unique to the PR
quizQuestions.explanation: Lead time = deploy_finished_at minus min(authored_at of commits unique to the PR); the median is reported over the window.

quizQuestions.question: For a squash merge, where should authored_at come from?
options: The PR's pre-merge commit history captured at ingestion
quizQuestions.explanation: Squash/rebase lose original authored timestamps on the merged commit, so use the PR's own pre-merge commit history captured at ingestion.

quizQuestions.question: Which message queue does the MVP use, and why?
quizQuestions.explanation: RabbitMQ is chosen for its retry/DLQ semantics out of the box (ADR-0002); Kafka is revisited at scale.

quizQuestions.question: What is the minimum audit-log retention requirement?
quizQuestions.explanation: Every config change, access grant, and export must be written to the audit log with 12+ month retention.

quizQuestions.question: When must an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) be written?
options: Only after a feature ships to production
Before or with any choice of framework, datastore, queue, protocol, or cross-cutting pattern
Only when a senior engineer requests one
quizQuestions.explanation: Architectural decisions require an ADR recorded before or with the implementing change; accepted ADRs are superseded, never silently deviated from.

quizQuestions.question: What does 'APIs are contract-first' require?
options: Write the code first, then generate docs
Update the OpenAPI spec before implementing endpoint changes
quizQuestions.explanation: The OpenAPI spec must be updated before implementing endpoint changes.

quizQuestions.question: How are individual-level views handled?
options: Always visible to managers by default
Opt-in, access-gated, and framed around growth, never ranking
quizQuestions.explanation: Individual views are opt-in, access-gated, and growth-framed; no metric ranks or shames an individual by default.

quizQuestions.question: What default threshold marks a PR as 'oversized'?
quizQuestions.explanation: PR size distribution flags oversized PRs at a default of >400 changed lines (additions + deletions).

quizQuestions.question: What is the frontend stack?
quizQuestions.explanation: Frontend is React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind with Recharts for visualization (ADR-0001).

quizQuestions.question: What is the dashboard load-time target?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dashboards must load in under 3 seconds at roughly 1M events, served from pre-aggregated mart tables.

quizQuestions.question: How should an unresolved contributor identity be handled?
options: Silently dropped to keep data clean
Flagged for Admin review, never dropped or double-counted
Merged automatically with the closest name
quizQuestions.explanation: Unresolved identities are flagged for Admin review/confirm/merge/split; they are never silently dropped or double-counted.

quizQuestions.question: Are bot accounts included in people-dimension metrics by default?
options: No, they are excluded by default
quizQuestions.explanation: Bot accounts are detected and excluded from people-dimension metrics by default.

quizQuestions.question: In the AI ROI formula, how is estimated_hours_saved computed?
options: commits per day * days in month
quizQuestions.explanation: hours_saved = ai_assisted_pr_count * (nonAi_cycle_p50 - ai_cycle_p50); dollar value = hours_saved * blended_hourly_rate; roi_multiple = value / total_ai_spend.

quizQuestions.question: How must ROI calculation assumptions like blended_hourly_rate be handled?
options: Org-configurable and shown alongside the figure
Set by the vendor of the AI tool
quizQuestions.explanation: Assumptions must be visible and adjustable, shown alongside the figure -- never presented as a hidden constant.

quizQuestions.question: Which commit-message convention does the repo follow?
options: Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, refactor:, test:, chore:)
quizQuestions.explanation: The repo uses Conventional Commits with trunk-based development and short-lived feature branches.

quizQuestions.question: Which code most requires unit tests, per the standards?
quizQuestions.explanation: Unit tests are required for all business logic, especially metric computations -- DORA math bugs destroy user trust.

quizQuestions.question: When a vendor API returns 429/5xx, what should a connector do?
options: Drop the events and move on
Back off (honoring Retry-After), queue-and-drain, and retry
Crash so an operator restarts it
Switch to writing directly to the mart
quizQuestions.explanation: Connectors back off honoring Retry-After and queue-and-drain; persistent failures raise a connector-health alert and poison messages go to the DLQ.

quizQuestions.question: What is the correct five-layer data flow?
options: Sources -> Ingestion -> Identity & Normalization -> Metrics/Semantic -> Application/API -> Presentation
quizQuestions.explanation: The flow is Sources -> Ingestion -> Identity & Normalization -> Metrics/Semantic -> Application/API -> Presentation.

quizQuestions.question: What data do connectors ingest about code?
options: Full source code bodies for analysis
Metadata only -- no source-code bodies or message contents
quizQuestions.explanation: The platform ingests metadata only -- no source-code bodies and no message contents -- per the security standards.

quizQuestions.question: How is a rollback deployment treated?
options: Counted as a deploy, and also flagged as a failure signal for CFR
quizQuestions.explanation: A rollback is a real deploy (counts toward frequency) but is also a failure signal for CFR; as the remediation it is excluded from the CFR failure numerator itself.

quizQuestions.question: When no events or metrics exist yet, what should minutesToValue return?
quizQuestions.explanation: Both timestamps are null until data exists, so minutesToValue and withinTarget stay null rather than defaulting to a misleading 0.

quizQuestions.question: Where may secrets and credentials be stored?
options: In config files committed to the repo
Env vars / secret manager only, encrypted at rest
quizQuestions.explanation: No secrets in code or config; use env vars / secret manager only, with encryption in transit and at rest.

quizQuestions.question: Which tool manages database migrations, and in what style?
quizQuestions.explanation: Flyway is used with forward-only, expand/contract migrations (ADR-0001).

quizQuestions.question: What makes metric numbers explainable and reproducible over time?
options: Metrics are recomputed randomly and cached
Append-only raw staging data plus versioned metric logic recorded with each value
Only the latest value is ever stored
Metrics are edited manually when they look wrong
quizQuestions.explanation: Every metric is reproducible from immutable staging, and the metric logic version is recorded with each computed value so history stays explainable.

quizQuestions.question: What must be preserved when a user drills from org to team?
options: The active filters and time range, plus breadcrumbs back up
quizQuestions.explanation: Drill-down preserves active filters and time range and provides breadcrumbs to navigate back up (E4-S2).

quizQuestions.question: What should a metric view show when there is no data?
options: An explanation (no data / out of range / still ingesting)
quizQuestions.explanation: Empty/loading states must explain themselves -- never a blank chart -- e.g. no data, out of range, or still ingesting.

quizQuestions.question: How is reviewer workload presented?
options: As an individual leaderboard ranking reviewers
As balance across the team, never an individual ranking
It is not shown at all
quizQuestions.explanation: Reviewer load is shown as balance across the team, never as an individual leaderboard, respecting the non-surveillance principle.

quizQuestions.question: What OAuth/API scopes should each connector request?
options: The minimum least-privilege read scopes needed
Write scopes so it can correct tool data
quizQuestions.explanation: Least-privilege integrations: request the minimum read-only scopes needed per connector.

quizQuestions.question: When is a code change considered complete in this repo?
options: When its documentation is updated in the same commit/PR
When a reviewer approves, docs optional
When it is merged, docs later
quizQuestions.explanation: Documentation is part of the definition of done -- no code change is complete until its docs are updated in the same commit/PR.

quizQuestions.question: What must accompany any new metric?
options: A metric definition (name, formula, sources, edge cases, BRD requirement)
quizQuestions.explanation: New metrics require an entry in docs/01-product/metric-definitions.md -- metric transparency is a trust requirement, not nice-to-have.

quizQuestions.question: What is the platform's deliberate positioning?
options: A replacement for Jira and GitHub
Automated no-tagging DORA/SPACE analytics with leadership-friendly UX, avoiding surveillance and a mandatory query language
quizQuestions.explanation: It occupies the middle ground: minware-style no-tagging analytics via Hivel-style leadership UX, avoiding surveillance and a mandatory query language.

quizQuestions.question: How are production deployments detected for DORA?
options: From CI/CD events via a per-repo configurable deploy workflow pattern
quizQuestions.explanation: Deployments are detected from CI/CD events using a per-repo configurable pattern (METRICS_DEPLOY_WORKFLOW_PATTERN) -- no manual tagging.

quizQuestions.question: A ticket with no linked PR is handled how in ticket lead time?
options: Counted with a lead time of zero
Excluded from the metric and reported in an 'unlinked work' quality indicator
quizQuestions.explanation: Tickets with no linked PR are excluded from ticket lead time and surfaced in an unlinked-work indicator feeding the Investment Profile.

quizQuestions.question: Which fields make up the standard event envelope (ADR-0003)?
quizQuestions.explanation: Connectors wrap payloads as {source, sourceId, eventType, receivedAt, connectorVersion, payload} before publishing to the queue.

quizQuestions.question: How is work classified as planned / unplanned / rework?
options: Engineers manually select a category per commit
By correlating Git activity to Jira epics via linkage heuristics (branch names, PR titles, smart commits)
quizQuestions.explanation: Classification comes from Jira<->Git linkage heuristics; unclassifiable work is bucketed transparently, never silently dropped -- consistent with zero-tagging.

quizQuestions.question: How is future multi-tenancy accommodated in the MVP schema?
options: It is impossible without a rewrite
A tenant-ID scoping is reserved in the schema from day one
Each tenant gets a separate database immediately
Tenancy is handled only in the frontend
quizQuestions.explanation: Tenant-ID scoping is reserved in the schema from day one for Phase 4 multi-tenancy, so commercialization needs no re-architecture.
